title: nested_branches always records "then" for a nested conditional, regardless of which inner branch actually fired
description: When the taken outer `.then()` contains a nested when-chain, lines 2098-2100 append `self.taken_branch` to `nested_branches` intending to capture the inner branch that fired. But `self._is_outer` was set False at line 2094 BEFORE `self.evaluate(then_node)` runs at line 2096, so the nested _eval_clauses invocation sees `is_outer=False` and never updates `self.taken_branch`. At line 2100 `self.taken_branch` is therefore still the outer's "then", and `self.taken_branch or 'then'` always appends "then". The inner-otherwise case is thus mislabelled as inner-then. nested_branches is surfaced to the trace UI (EvaluatedExpression.nested_branches -> dataclasses.asdict). The intended semantics (record the inner branch kind) are never achievable with the current ordering.
evidence: Executed repro. Code: out=pl.when(pl.col('a')>0).then(pl.when(pl.col('b')>0).then(1).otherwise(2)).otherwise(3). With a=1,b=-1 the inner OTHERWISE fires (result_value=2, confirmed via _compute_result_impl), yet _evaluate_conditional_branches returns nested_branches=['then'] (expected ['otherwise']). With a=1,b=1 (inner then) it also returns ['then'] — so the field is constant 'then' whenever a nested-in-then conditional is taken, carrying no real information. Additionally, a nested when inside the OTHERWISE branch is never recorded in nested_branches at all (the append only exists in the cond/then path), confirmed: a=-1,b=1 gives nested_branches=[].
